title: 10.4 A 2- TRX IR-UWB Transceiver with Shared Antennas Supporting Channels 5 to 12 in Compliance with IEEE 802.15.4/4z Standards
problem: IR-UWB transceivers must support multiple channels (5-12) to reduce interference in crowded 6GHz spectrum while minimizing cost through antenna sharing, but previous integrated RF switches suffer high insertion loss degrading receiver sensitivity.
motivation: UWB IoT/mobile/automotive expansion creates multi-user interference in congested spectrum; supporting multiple channels requires efficient integration while sharing antennas to reduce BOM cost.
method: Fully integrated 2-TRX IR-UWB transceiver with multi-channel support (channels 5-12), using integrated CMOS RF switches optimized to reduce insertion loss while supporting shared TX/RX antenna architecture per IEEE 802.15.4/4z.
key_novelty: Optimized integrated RF switch design reducing insertion loss and noise figure degradation compared to prior CMOS implementations, enabling multi-channel shared-antenna operation.
contributions: Fully integrated RF switches eliminating external SOI switches and SiP cost
Reduced insertion loss and noise figure vs prior CMOS switch implementations
primary_theme: integrated multi-channel IR-UWB transceiver with shared antennas
